messages.author: 4d78542ee90d0285
messages.subject: Problems computing posterior predictives
parts:
Hello blavaan users,


I've been getting problems after updating R to the last version 3.6.0, blavaan package starts compiling and running the chains properly, but when it finishes estimating the chains and starts "Computing posterior predictives ..."  the task stops (task manager says there is not any big job from R), but R looks like running the step but it is not doing anything. I'm a Arch Linux user and already tested the package in another Archlinux installation and it works fine, so I believe my Linux installation is missing something but I cannot detect what it is. This problem happens even with a simple model like this:



library(blavaan)
library(rstan)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              '


fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
            target="stan", std.lv=T, mcmcfile = T)
summary(fit)
 



The same problem happens with JAGS and STAN, but if I run the model using runjags or rstan, it works totally fine.


Any idea  or recommendation? I will appreciate any help.

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Problems computing posterior predictives
parts:
Esteban,

I am uncertain, but my first guess is that there is an issue with
parallelization. This is because some of the posterior predictive
computations use mclapply(). You might add the argument

test="none"

to see whether that works. That would help narrow down where the
problem could be arising. Also, I don't know why it would matter, but
you might try removing the options(mc.cores...) line. Let me know
whether either of those help.

Ed

Hi Ed,

Thanks for your prompt answer. After setting test = "none", the model runs in JAGS and STAN, but I'm getting this warning form Stan that I don't get in different Linux installations:


1: There were 1 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth. Increase max_treedepth above 10. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#maximum-treedepth-exceeded
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

I believe I can ignore this warning ?


It seems there is something happening , as you said, in the mcapply function, I will try to check it in the source code and see if I can detect any particular problem.

messages.subject: Re: Problems computing posterior predictives
parts:
Hello Ed and Mauricio,

I just wanted to do a follow up regarding my problem. I've found the solution to my problem. 

I had installed the library 'openblas' instead of 'blas'. For some reason that I don't understand yet, the version of package for linear algebra affected the estimation of posterior predictive and tests that were programmed. This is a weird finding given that I've been using openblas for years in Arch Linux and I've never had a problem with R because of this.

Thanks Ed and Mauricio for your help.
El viernes, 10 de mayo de 2019, 14:29:35 (UTC-5), Mauricio Garnier-Villarreal escribió:

Esteban

Your example code as is, works fine in my Ubuntu machine. The only difference in versions is that I have the development blavaan_0.3-5.410



On Friday, May 10, 2019 at 2:11:51 PM UTC-5, Ed Merkle wrote:
Esteban,

I am uncertain, but my first guess is that there is an issue with
parallelization. This is because some of the posterior predictive
computations use mclapply(). You might add the argument

test="none"

to see whether that works. That would help narrow down where the
problem could be arising. Also, I don't know why it would matter, but
you might try removing the options(mc.cores...) line. Let me know
whether either of those help.

Ed

Hi All,

Is there a way around setting test = "none"? This is because fitMeasures do not work when this done and I can't get PPP values for my model.

I'm using a Windows 10 Desktop, R version 3.5.0, blavaan 0.3-4, and rstan  version 2.18.2. Even with no parallel computing and R version 3.6.0, "Computing posterior predictives" looks like it's running forever.

Thanks,
John

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Problems computing posterior predictives
parts:
John

If you set test="none", you will not get any value that comes from the log-likelohoods (or marginal LL). This is because you are asking to skip that step

Factors that affect the time of calculation: complexity of your model, sample size, number of saved samples, missing data. You cannot change the model or sample size, you can control the number of saved samples, if you are now saving 10000 samples per chain, I would recommend to change it to 2000 for example, this was the posterior predictive calculation time will be shorter
